sections.heading: What is a Trie?
sections.content: A Trie (pronounced 'try', also called a prefix tree) is a tree that stores strings one character per edge. All words that share a prefix share the same path from the root, so the prefix is stored only once. Each node can mark whether a word ends there. A trie answers 'does this word exist?' and 'does any word start with this prefix?' in O(L) time, where L is the length of the query, independent of how many words are stored.

sections.heading: When to Use It
items: Prefix search and autocomplete (words that start with 'app')
Check whether a word or a prefix exists in a dictionary
Search with wildcards such as '.' in a word dictionary
Search many words in a grid at once (Word Search II)
Replace words by their shortest root, or find the longest common prefix
Count how many words share a prefix
Binary tries for maximum XOR and bitwise prefix problems
Keywords: prefix, startsWith, dictionary, autocomplete, suggestions, wildcard, longest prefix

sections.heading: The Intuition
sections.content: Imagine the words 'cat', 'car' and 'cart'. A HashSet stores three separate strings. A trie stores one path c, a, t and one path c, a, r, and 'cart' simply extends the 'car' path by one more node. The shared prefix 'ca' exists once. To check whether any word starts with 'ca', you walk two edges and you are done, with no need to scan every word.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
items: Forgetting the isEnd flag, so 'car' is wrongly reported as a word when only 'cart' was inserted
Returning true from search when you should check isEnd (search needs isEnd, startsWith does not)
Using an array of 26 for input that contains uppercase letters, digits or symbols
Using the trie for exact-match-only queries where a HashSet is simpler and lighter
Not copying the path when collecting words in DFS (use StringBuilder and delete the last character)
Adding duplicate results in Word Search II (clear the stored word after it is found)
Underestimating memory: 26 pointers per node can be heavy for large, sparse dictionaries
Forgetting to handle the empty string and the null child cases

sections.heading: Key Takeaways
items: A trie stores strings character by character so words with the same prefix share a path
Insert, search and prefix queries cost O(L), independent of the number of stored words
Use isEnd to tell complete words from prefixes
Use an array of 26 for lowercase letters and a HashMap for larger alphabets
Store extra data in nodes (counts, the word, top suggestions) to answer harder questions in O(L)
Pair a trie with DFS or backtracking for wildcard search and for searching many words in a grid
